description: A version is proposed only once it has been public for seven days, so that a release pulled or fixed in its first week never reaches a branch. internalChecksFilter is already strict by default; it is stated so that the wait is read here as holding back the branch and the pull request themselves, not only a status check on them

packageRules.description: Patches, digest updates and the first pins are merged by Renovate itself once the pull request's checks pass (ci.yml). Minor and major updates change what is promised and are only opened. The repository allows no auto-merge of its own, so Renovate merges rather than the platform, and only after the checks it can see have succeeded

The netns testbed's base image is pulled by a tag that is pushed again whenever its Debian layer or Go patch is rebuilt, so a checkout does not say which image a run used. Pinning the digest makes the Dockerfile name one image and leaves Renovate to move it

The go directive in go.mod is the Go the checks run (setup-go reads it) and the golang image is the Go the netns tests run in. They are the same minor on purpose: a test passing on one Go says little about another. Grouping them puts both on one branch, so they cannot drift apart one pull request at a time

A new Go minor (the go directive and the golang image) waits for approval on the dashboard, since raising the go directive raises what every user of the module must build with; patches and digests flow as usual

Workflows are already read by the github-actions manager. Grouping them keeps a handful of actions from arriving as a handful of pull requests, since they are updated together and reviewed the same way
